operator_io_quirks: All identifiers are mixed-case with underscores (Company_ID, Rank_of_the_Year); must be double-quoted in generated SQL.
DDL uses backticks in FK clauses (`Station_ID`) while table/column defs use double quotes; sqlite_master text must be replayed verbatim.
Tiny tables: company=10, gas_station=11, station_company=6 rows; original_values fully captured, no sampling needed.
station_company has composite PK (Station_ID, Company_ID) and two FKs to two different parents; both parents exist and are unique.

FK parent columns are the PKs of company/gas_station, so parent values are unique; child FK draws with replacement will create duplicate (Station_ID,Company_ID) pairs that get dropped by sample_fresh_primary_keys.
No NOT NULL, no CHECK, no UNIQUE constraints anywhere; only PKs and FKs. Insert failures will be rare (only PK collisions).
Open_Year is declared INT and stored as integer (1998..2003); TS dispatches to Number, not Date — no date fuzzer involved.
Sales/Profits/Assets/Market_Value are REAL with values up to 2550.0; Number fuzzer with scale=0 (no args) will draw from [-1,1] and perturb by ±1/±2, wildly off-scale.
Rank and Rank_of_the_Year are small ints (1..10); Number fuzzer will produce values far outside this range.
Text columns contain spaces, trailing spaces ('James Colin ', 'Rob Jefferies '), and concatenated names ('BrianWingrave'); String fuzzer's contaminate step will add more noise.
Headquarters distinct=5, Main_Industry distinct=3 — low-cardinality categorical columns; TS String fuzzer will not preserve the small domain.
No views, triggers, or indexes beyond PKs; DDL replay is simple.
operator_ts_expectations: Number fuzzer on Company_ID/Station_ID (INT, no args): scale=0, range [-1,1], int perturbation ±1/±2 — PKs will be tiny and collide often, causing many dropped rows in sample_fresh_primary_keys.

Number fuzzer on Sales_billion etc. (REAL, no args): scale=0, range [-1,1], float perturbation ±0.01/±0.02 — values will be ~0, never near the real 100-2500 range; queries filtering Sales_billion > 100 will return empty on generated instances (FN driver).
Number fuzzer on Open_Year: draws from [-1,1] plus perturbation — years like 0, -1, 2; queries with Open_Year BETWEEN 1998 AND 2003 will be empty (FN driver).

String fuzzer on Company/Headquarters/Main_Industry: 5 original samples + literal pool, p=0.2 fresh random strings over a-zA-Z0-9() of length 0-20, then 50% contaminate — will produce garbage like 'xK3(' mixed with real names; equality/IN queries on these columns will mostly miss (FN).
String fuzzer on Manager_Name etc.: same; trailing-space originals preserved as elements, so 'James Colin ' vs 'James Colin' ties may appear (FP driver for = comparisons).

station_company FK columns draw from parent's FINAL filtered values with replacement; since parents are tiny (10-11 rows) and PKs collide, parent may end up with very few rows, so FK columns get few distinct values — joins may be sparse.
Composite PK (Station_ID,Company_ID) in station_company: sample_fresh_primary_keys drops duplicate pairs; with tiny parent domains, many rows dropped, table may shrink to a handful.
No unique columns besides PKs, so drop_unique_duplicates is a no-op here.

choose_table_sizes: level 0 (company, gas_station) gets 1+30*u rows, level 1 (station_company) gets 4x that capped at 2500 — station_company will be much larger than its parents, amplifying FK duplication and PK-drop.
Literal pool from train SQL will seed real company names, locations, years into the samplers, partially mitigating the garbage — but only for columns that appear in train queries.

Overall: TS will produce instances where numeric range predicates (Sales, Open_Year, Rank) are almost always empty and string equality is mostly noise — classic FN pattern; ties from trailing spaces and duplicate FK draws give occasional FP.
